data.command: Describe UNC2452 SolarWinds supply chain attack

data.text:
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ cat /usr/share/doc/threat-intel/unc2452-advisory.txt

UNC2452 / SolarWinds Supply Chain Compromise
Threat intel note - last updated by secops
Source designations: UNC2452 (Mandiant/FireEye), Dark Halo (Volexity),
StellarParticle (CrowdStrike), SolarStorm, NOBELIUM (Microsoft); attributed
to APT29 / Cozy Bear, assessed as Russian SVR.

WHAT HAPPENED
A threat actor gained access to the build environment of SolarWinds and
inserted code into the Orion IT monitoring platform before it was compiled
and code-signed. Because the implant shipped inside a legitimately signed
update, every customer that applied it received a backdoor from what looked
like a trusted vendor channel. Disclosed December 2020; roughly 18,000
customers are believed to have downloaded the trojanized build.

STAGE 1 - SUNBURST / Solorigate backdoor
- Payload: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (also tracked as
  SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.ORIONSYSTEMS backdoor).
- Affected builds: Orion Platform 2019.4 HF5, 2020.2, 2020.2 HF1 and
  nearby hotfixes; signed with a valid SolarWinds certificate.
- The DLL sat dormant for roughly 12-14 days after installation, then
  generated a fake "Orion Improvement Program" HTTP request to
  avsvmcloud[.]com with a base64/DGA-encoded path containing host and
  domain fingerprint data.
- Anti-forensics: checked for security, endpoint, and sandbox vendor
  indicators in process names, services, and DNS suffixes (e.g. products
  from Microsoft, CrowdStrike, FireEye, Palo Alto, SentinelOne, Carbon
  Black, ESET, F-Secure, Sophos, Bitdefender and others). If a match was
  found the implant would not run.
- Tasking supported file transfer, process execution, system profiling
  (users, groups, local admins, services), and system reboot.

STAGE 2 - hands-on-keyboard tooling
- TEARDROP: memory-only dropper that decrypted and loaded a Cobalt Strike
  Beacon; delivered via the staged backdoor.
- RAINDROP: alternative loader observed on a smaller set of victims.
- Cobalt Strike used for internal recon and lateral movement.

IDENTITY AND CLOUD ABUSE
- Golden SAML: forged SAML tokens signed with the stolen ADFS token
  signing certificate, allowing impersonation of any federated identity
  without knowing passwords and largely bypassing MFA.
- Persistence in Azure AD/Office 365 by adding credentials or role
  assignments to existing service principals and applications.
- Stolen token signing keys and mailbox access used to read mail and files
  from cloud tenants; targets included US government departments
  (Treasury, State, Commerce, DHS, NIH, DOJ) and multiple technology firms.
- On-prem credentials dumped from local systems and deployed into cloud
  environments where those accounts were reused (password spraying against
  valid-but-unenforced accounts).

DETECTION / IOCs (abbreviated)
- Network: DNS to avsvmcloud[.]com and related DGA-style domains;
  outbound HTTP to previously unseen infrastructure from Orion servers.
- Host: unusual DLL loading by the Orion process tree; named pipes;
  presence of files/hashes published in Mandiant's SUNBURST countermeasures.
- Cloud: SAML token issuance anomalies, new credentials added to existing
  service principals, atypical mailbox delegation and mailbox search rules.

MITIGATION
- Upgrade Orion to vendor-fixed releases (2020.2.1 HF1/HF2 and later).
- Rotate every credential the Orion server could reach, and rotate the
  ADFS/token signing certificates. Where signing keys cannot be proven
  intact, rebuild ADFS and re-issue tokens.
- Invalidate refresh tokens and sessions, audit mail-forwarding and
  application consent grants, review service principal credentials.
- Audit and harden the software build pipeline: signing key custody,
  least privilege for build agents, reproducible builds, artifact review.
